flagged.evidence: [F1] says the Fourier coefficients identify smooth periodic fields with rapidly decreasing coefficient families, and step 3.1 says smooth initial data make the weighted sums finite for every integer m. The cited `def-fd-periodic-fourier-sobolev-spaces` only defines H^s as a weighted coefficient completion; it does not establish smooth periodic fields belong to every H^m. Parseval applied to derivatives, or repeated integration by parts, closes this short gap.

The current carrier cites Golse §7.4. In the cited PDF, the contents label §7.4 “The compressible Euler system”; the acoustic system is in §2.3 and its Cauchy problem in §7.1.2. Thus §7.4 is an inaccurate locator for the acoustic result cited here.
